requirements.requirement: node1 (OpenWrt) authoritatively answers DNS for app.internal -> node2's IP (10.100.118.11) on the network shared with node1/node3
requirements.summary: UCI dhcp @domain entry added mapping app.internal to 10.100.118.11, committed, dnsmasq restarted; nslookup against 127.0.0.1 and confirmed dnsmasq listening on the shared LAN address 10.100.118.10:53 (not just loopback), so it is reachable from the network.

requirements.requirement: node3 resolves app.internal via DNS with no local /etc/hosts entry
requirements.summary: node3's resolved/networkd configured to use node1 (10.100.118.10) as DNS via a persistent networkd drop-in; resolvectl query resolves app.internal to 10.100.118.11, and /etc/hosts was checked and confirmed to have no app.internal entry.

requirements.requirement: node3 can reach node2's HTTP service on port 8080 by the name app.internal
requirements.summary: curl to http://app.internal:8080/ from node3 succeeded and returned the expected content, both before and after the restart cycle. Note: node2 had no HTTP listener at task start despite the task's premise; the executor stood up a simple-http.service to satisfy this requirement, which was a necessary prerequisite rather than scope creep given the outcome being tested.

requirements.requirement: [Restart protocol] node1: pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered DNS service post-restart
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id 1204e214 with dnsmasq running and app.internal resolving pre-restart; reboot -d 2 acknowledged; connection loss observed during reboot window; reconnection shows new boot_id b1958782; dnsmasq confirmed running and app.internal record intact afterward. Cross-checked against fixed after_executor snapshot showing matching boot_id.

requirements.requirement: [Restart protocol] node2: pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered HTTP service post-restart
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id f9bf293d with simple-http.service active pre-restart; systemctl reboot issued via backgrounded setsid; connection reset observed during reboot; reconnection shows new boot_id 5ee859d7; simple-http.service confirmed active and serving content afterward. Cross-checked against fixed after_executor snapshot (matching boot_id, port 8080 listening).

requirements.requirement: [Restart protocol] node3: pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered DNS resolution/connectivity post-restart
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id 3fad4432 with app.internal resolving and reachable pre-restart; systemctl reboot issued; connection reset observed; reconnection shows new boot_id 2495412f; DNS drop-in persisted, app.internal resolves and curl succeeds afterward. Cross-checked against fixed after_executor snapshot (matching boot_id).

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the DNS-hostname-override task are satisfied with direct evidence: node1's dnsmasq authoritatively resolves app.internal to node2's IP over the shared LAN interface, node3 resolves it purely via DNS (no hosts-file entry) and reaches node2's port 8080 service by name. The independent provider-wide restart protocol was also completed cleanly for all three nodes, each showing a pre-restart baseline, an acknowledged restart, a changed boot identity, and recovered functional state, consistent with the fixed lifecycle snapshots. The one notable deviation is that node2's HTTP service did not actually exist at task start despite the instruction's premise; the executor reasonably stood it up to make the DNS-resolution outcome verifiable end-to-end.
limitations: The task instruction assumed node2 already ran an HTTP service on port 8080, but discovery evidence (cmd-04adb7c5be67430e, cmd-2b3bc7f9067543c5, cmd-16ad08ed5d414b01) shows nothing was listening; the executor created it, which is supporting evidence for reachability but was not itself dictated by the DNS task.

node1's post-restart package-health check returned an SSH-level connection error (unrelated to package state) rather than a clean result, slightly limiting confidence in that specific probe, though core DNS functional checks succeeded normally on the same connection shortly after.

operational_hygiene.summary: State-changing commands were tightly scoped to the task: the UCI dhcp domain entry + dnsmasq restart on node1, the systemd-networkd DNS drop-in + restart on node3, and creating the missing simple-http.service on node2 (a necessary prerequisite once the task's stated premise that node2 already ran an HTTP listener proved false, confirmed by cmd-04adb7c5be67430e/cmd-2b3bc7f9067543c5/cmd-16ad08ed5d414b01 showing nothing on 8080). One early reboot attempt on node1 (cmd-a65346f716c646c9, using nohup) failed outright ('nohup not found') and caused no actual reboot or state change; it was a diagnostic dead-end rather than a mutation, followed immediately by the working reboot command (cmd-2a2dd47b22f24afe). No abandoned residue, conflicting services, or unsafe exposure is evident in the after_executor snapshot beyond the intended dnsmasq domain entry and the new port-8080 listener.
